file_name: E and H - 2004 - Procuring a usable system using unemployed personas.txt

barriers.description: A very tight project schedule imposed by the procurement project group (PPG) limited the time available for user research, iteration, and stakeholder involvement.
barriers.justification: The compressed timeline hindered the ability to conduct thorough user research, multiple iterations, and deep stakeholder engagement, directly impacting the process-level workloads of integrating feedback & iteration and facilitating user involvement.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The project group had worked for five months nailing down the organizational requirements and their time was running out. ... Therefore the UCD process could not take more than eight weeks. At the same time they wanted two iterations and a thorough interview phase. Hence, the schedule for the UCD process was very tight.

barriers.description: The PPG's lack of detailed understanding of user requirements and the design process led to a halt in the project, disrupting the design team's workflow.
barriers.justification: This knowledge gap prevented effective coordination and shared understanding, directly impeding the process-level workload of coordinating a multidisciplinary team and integrating feedback & iteration.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The PPG had not been able to follow and understand all the decisions that had been taken during the design process. Therefore they were also not sure about the connection between their abstract organizational goals and the now concrete design. We were assigned to lead a series of full-day workshops with the PPG to backtrack what had been done and work through both the organizational and user requirements again.

barriers.description: The organizational requirements provided by the PPG were abstract, sometimes contradictory, and not sufficiently detailed to guide design decisions.
barriers.justification: This lack of actionable requirements hindered the operational workload of specifying user and organizational requirements and the process-level workload of addressing the holistic experience.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Of course, there were still questions that were unanswered and even some contradictions in the documents on organizational requirements, but we expected these to be resolved during the second iteration.

barriers.description: The PPG felt uncomfortable and insufficiently involved in the fast-paced design process, leading to uncertainty and a lack of confidence in the results.
barriers.justification: This emotional discomfort reduced effective collaboration and hindered the process-level workload of coordinating a multidisciplinary team and integrating feedback & iteration.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Things happened very fast. And I don’t think we were prepared on that. (…) So we felt that we were maybe not really involved in all the details of the work, which we may have wanted to be. ... But when you look back at it we should have spent more time in the project and been more involved.
